# Library

Books, papers, reference entries, notes and course material, organised by domain, then subject, then document type.

## Layout

```
Library/<Domain>/<Subject>/<Doc type>/<file>
```

| Domain | Subjects |
|---|---|
| Humanities | Philosophy (includes anthropology, sociology, economics, linguistics), Psychoanalysis, Religion, History, Politics |
| Science & Maths | Maths, Physics, Robotics |
| Computing | ML, Programming, DevOps, Hardware |
| Fiction | Literature |

A subject only gets a doc-type folder when it has files of that type.

| Doc type | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| Books | Monographs, textbooks, edited volumes, fiction. A series gets its own subfolder (e.g. `Physics/Books/Feynman Special Lectures/`) |
| Papers | Journal articles, preprints, working papers, reports, standalone essays |
| Reference | Encyclopedia entries (SEP, IEP), dictionaries, handbooks and handbook chapters, companions |
| Notes | University lecture notes and course handouts that stand on their own |
| Courses | Whole courses: `Courses/<course>-<institution>-<year>/` with `slides/`, `notes/`, `videos/`, `exercises/` and `solutions/` |

## File names

```
<title>-<authors>-<year>.<ext>
```

1. Lowercase only. Words are joined with single hyphens. Punctuation, brackets and quotes are removed.
2. Authors are separated by hyphens. Three or more authors become `<first-author>-et-al`. Organisations use a short name (`cia`, `ilo`, `amnesty-international`).
3. Encyclopedia entries use the source in place of the author: `metaphysics-sep-2023.pdf`, `slavoj-zizek-iep.pdf`.
4. The year is the original publication year when it can be verified (`black-skin-white-masks-frantz-fanon-1952.epub`). If it can't be verified, leave it out.
5. Handbook chapters carry the handbook and chapter: `oxford-handbook-epistemology-of-theology-ch1-knowledge-of-god-john-greco-2017.pdf`.
6. Course files keep their lecture numbers: `14-2-view-geometry.pdf`.

## Embedded metadata

Every PDF and EPUB carries its metadata inside the file, so readers and search tools see it.

- PDF (written with `exiftool`): `Title`, `Author` (`; `-separated), `Subject` = `<Subject> / <Doc type>`, `Keywords` and XMP `dc:subject` = the tags.
- EPUB (written with Calibre `ebook-meta`): title, authors, published date, tags.
- Tags always start with `<Domain>, <Subject>, <Doc type>`, followed by topic tags (`deleuze-guattari`, `minimum-wage`, `masculinity`) and `isbn:<13 digits>` where one is known.

Known untagged files: `anti-oedipus-capitalism-and-schizophrenia-...-1977.pdf` (DRM-encrypted) and `27-advanced-dense-3d-reconstruction.pdf` (broken xref table).

## Where it lives

This iCloud folder is the master copy. `~/Drive/My Drive/Library/` in Google Drive is a mirror for Colab and other Google tools, refreshed every 15 minutes by `~/.local/bin/icloud-to-gdrive` (launch agent `com.tom.icloud-to-gdrive`, log in `~/.local/state/icloud-to-gdrive.log`). The same job mirrors `Admin`, `Print`, `Reference`, `Study` and `Work`.

Add, rename, move and delete files here only. Anything changed only in the Drive copy is overwritten or deleted on the next sync.

## Adding a file

1. Identify the title, authors and year from the file's metadata or first page.
2. Rename it using the convention above.
3. Place it in `<Domain>/<Subject>/<Doc type>/`.
4. Tag it:
   ```
   exiftool -overwrite_original_in_place -Title="..." -Author="A; B" \
     -Subject="Philosophy / Papers" -Keywords="Humanities, Philosophy, Papers, topic" FILE.pdf
   ebook-meta FILE.epub --title "..." --authors "A & B" --tags "Humanities,Philosophy,Books,topic" --date 1952-01-01
   ```

the 'internalization' of the historically specified ideological agencies,

and tries to integrate the Oedipus complex int o the totality of the social

process of production and reproduction. However, members of the

Frankfurt School, particularly Theodor Adorno and Herbert Marcuse,

fought this 'revisionist' tendency fr om the very beginning in. the name

of a strict historical-materialist approach: at stake in the so-called

Kulturismus-Debatte, the first great splitting within the Franrt School,

was precisely the repudiation of Fromm's neo-Freudian revisionism.

What, then, were the Frankfurt School's objections to this revisionist

attempt to 'socialize' Freud by shifting the accent from the libidinal

conflict between Ego and Id to the social-ethical conflicts within the Ego?

While 'revisionism' replaces 'nature' ('archaic', 'pre-individual' drives)

with 'culture' (the creative potential of the individual, his alienation in

contemporary 'mass society'), for Adorno and Marcuse, the true

problem resides in this 'nature' itse In what appears as 'nature', as

biological or, at least, philogenetic heritage, critical analysis must

unearth the traces of historical mediation. Psychic 'natue' is the result

of a historical process which, on account of the alienated character of

history, assumes the 'reified', 'naturalized' form of its opposite, of a pre

historical given state of things:

 

The 'sub-individual and pre-individual factors' that define the individual

belong to the realm of the archaic and biological; but it is not a question of

pure nature. Rather it is second nature: history that has hardened into nature.

The distinction between nature and second nature, if unfamiliar to most

social thought, is vital to critical theory. What is second nature to the

individual is accumulated and sedimented history. It is history so long

unliberated - history so long monotonously oppressive - that it congeals.

Second nature is not simply nature or history, but frozen history that surfaces

as nature.s

 

10

 

THE DEADLOCK OF 'REPRESSIVE DESUBLIMATION'

 

Such 'historicizing' of the Freudian theoretical edifice has nothing in

cQmmon with fo cusing on sociocultural problems, on the Ego's moral

and emotional conflicts: rather, it stands squarely against the revisionist

gesture of 'domesticating' the unconscious - that is, of attenuating the

fundamental and irresolvable tension between the Ego, which is struc

tured according to the social norms, and the unconscious drives, which

are opposed to the Ego - the very tension that confers on Freud's theory

its critical potential. In an alienated society, the domain of 'culture' is

founded upon the violent exclusion ('repression') of man's libidinal

kernel which then assumes the form of a quasi-'nature': 'second nature'

is the petrified evidence of the price paid for 'cultural progress', the

barbarity inherent to 'culture' itself, Such a 'hieroglyphic' reading,

which detects in the quasi-biological repository of drives the traces of

congealed history, was practised above all by Marcuse:

 

Unlike the revisionists Marcuse holds to' Freud's quasi-biological concepts,

but more faithfully than Freud himself - and against Freud, unfolds them.

The revisionists introduce history, a social dynamic, into psychoanalysis from,

as it were, the outside- by social values, norms, goals. Marcuse finds the history

inside the concepts. He interprets Freud's 'biologism' as second nature,

petrified history.4
